name: ServiceTitan
tagline: All-in-one operations platform for home and commercial trades: dispatch, scheduling, pricebook, invoicing, payroll, marketing attribution.

pricing.basis: quote-based, typically per technician per month plus onboarding
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. ServiceTitan does not publish list pricing.

verdictSummary: This is not a personal app, it is the nervous system of an HVAC or plumbing company with trucks, techs, and payroll. The thing people pay for is not the calendar view, it is call recording tied to job outcomes, a maintained pricebook, credit card and consumer financing rails, GPS and dispatch, timesheets that feed payroll, and QuickBooks sync that an accountant will sign off on. An agent can build you a job tracker in an afternoon; it cannot build the money movement, the audit trail, or the twelve integrations the office manager already depends on. And nobody rips out the system that holds five years of customer equipment history and open invoices to try a homegrown one. If you are a solo tradesperson who has never paid for this, a local build is genuinely fine; if you have six techs, don't.
coreLoopDIY: A local job tracker for a one or two person trade business: customers, equipment, scheduled jobs, line-item estimates, and printable invoices in a single SQLite app.
requirements: a machine or small VPS that stays on
your own pricebook entered by hand
a separate payment processor if you want to take cards
whatYouLose: Payments, consumer financing, and payroll-grade timesheets
Dispatch board, GPS tracking, and technician mobile app that works offline in a crawlspace
Call recording and marketing attribution that tells you which ad paid for the job
Accounting sync that survives an audit, plus sales tax handling
Anyone to call at 7am when dispatch is down and eight trucks are idle
moatNotes: The pricebook, five years of equipment history, and open receivables are all hostages. That is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative is a whiteboard, three spreadsheets, and a dispatcher who quits. ServiceTitan is expensive and widely grumbled about, but it consolidates dispatch, invoicing, payments, financing, payroll input, and accounting into one place where the money actually reconciles at the end of the month. A self-hosted job tracker replaces the visible ten percent and leaves you personally responsible for the ninety percent that involves other people's money, other people's hours, and a state tax authority.
notes: A job list is a weekend; a business operating system is not. The moat is switching costs plus every integration that touches money: payments, financing, payroll, and the accountant's ledger.
prompt:
Build a local-first job management app for a solo tradesperson (HVAC, plumbing, electrical). This is a consolation build, not a ServiceTitan clone.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/jobs.db
- Drizzle ORM with a migration script
- No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services. Single operator on localhost or a private VPS.

Data model:
- customers: name, phone, email, address, notes
- equipment: belongs to customer, type, make, model, serial, install date, warranty end
- pricebook_items: code, name, description, unit price, taxable flag
- jobs: customer, optional equipment, status (lead, scheduled, in_progress, complete, invoiced, paid), scheduled_at, arrival window, description, private tech notes
- job_lines: job, pricebook item or freeform, qty, unit price, computed total
- payments: job, amount, method (cash, check, external card), date, reference

Screens:
- Today: jobs scheduled for today and tomorrow, sorted by window, one click to mark in_progress or complete
- Week calendar: simple 7 column grid, drag not required, click a day to schedule
- Customer detail: contact info, equipment list, full job history
- Job detail: add line items from the pricebook with search, live subtotal, one configurable tax rate from .env, notes field
- Pricebook CRUD with CSV import and export

Invoicing:
- Render an invoice as a print-optimized HTML route at /invoice/[jobId], styled for A4, browser print to PDF is fine
- Business name, address, and tax rate come from .env
- Track balance due as invoice total minus payments

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: card processing, financing, payroll, GPS, SMS or email sending, a mobile app, multi-user roles, accounting sync.

Include a seed script with 5 customers and 20 pricebook items, a README with setup in under 6 commands, and a nightly cron-friendly script that copies the SQLite file to ./backups with a date stamp.
